description: Evaluation-only synthetic hard-negative corpus for candidate-stage retrieval benchmarking. English documents intentionally overlap within topic clusters; Chinese, English, mixed-language, and exact-token queries test lexical, vector, rewrite, and RRF behavior. Never treat this corpus as production device truth.

documents.title: Prolonged Device Offline Troubleshooting Procedure
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. For a device that has remained offline for a prolonged period, troubleshoot in this order: verify power supply, verify SIM and data-plan status, check cellular coverage, then inspect firmware and runtime health. The procedure is diagnostic guidance and is not proof of a root cause.

documents.title: Offline Duration Threshold Policy
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. A prolonged-offline duration threshold is deployment policy, not a universal constant. A tenant or product may configure a duration before the platform labels a device prolonged offline. This document intentionally provides no concrete tenant value.

documents.title: Offline Alarm Debounce Policy
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Offline alarms may apply debounce, repeated-observation windows, notification suppression, and recovery clearing. Alarm policy controls notification behavior and does not define the troubleshooting order or establish a hardware root cause.

documents.title: Historical Offline Statistics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Historical offline statistics aggregate availability periods, disconnect counts, downtime duration, and recovery time. Historical statistics describe past behavior and do not specify the current troubleshooting sequence.

documents.title: shadowStatus CONFLICT Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. shadowStatus CONFLICT means the reported device state and the desired platform shadow state disagree. It is a state-consistency indicator. CONFLICT alone does not prove the device is offline, the broker failed, or a write command failed.

documents.title: Device Shadow Resynchronization
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Shadow resynchronization re-reads authoritative device state and reconciles desired and reported values after a mismatch. Resynchronization is a recovery workflow, not the definition of shadowStatus CONFLICT.

documents.title: Device Shadow Persistence Model
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Device shadow persistence stores desired state, reported state, update timestamps, and revision metadata. This evaluation passage intentionally does not name a concrete MySQL table or physical schema.

documents.title: Device Command Submission and Verification
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Successful command submission is not the same as verified device state. After a write command, query authoritative device state with bounded verification attempts. If the expected state is not observed, report verification timeout or mismatch instead of claiming success.

documents.title: SignalStrength Field Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. SignalStrength is a stored telemetry field. SignalStrength=0 means the stored field value is zero. Without protocol-specific encoding and freshness rules, zero alone must not be promoted to confirmed no-signal, modem failure, or disconnection.

documents.title: Signal Strength Calibration and Units
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Signal calibration maps raw modem measurements to protocol-specific signal units such as RSSI or RSRP. The mapping and valid ranges depend on the device protocol. This passage intentionally provides no universal conversion formula.

documents.title: Weak Signal Alarm Threshold Policy
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Weak-signal alarms compare fresh signal measurements with a configured threshold and may require consecutive breaches before alerting. Alarm thresholds are policy and do not define the semantic meaning of SignalStrength=0.

documents.title: SIM and Cellular Connectivity Diagnosis
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. For cellular connectivity diagnosis, verify SIM presence and activation, data-plan validity, account suspension, cellular coverage, and modem registration. This passage intentionally does not define a carrier HTTP API endpoint.

documents.title: PeripheralStatus Bit Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. PeripheralStatus uses binary flags in this corpus: bit0 is the lure-lamp circuit and bit1 is the camera circuit. For each defined bit, 0 means inactive and 1 means active. No semantics are defined for bit7.

documents.title: Peripheral Capability Matrix
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. A product capability matrix states whether a device model supports camera, lure lamp, environmental sensor, or other peripherals. Capability means supported hardware or function, not the current 0/1 state of PeripheralStatus.

documents.title: Peripheral Health Diagnosis
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Peripheral health diagnosis checks supply voltage, communication response, recent state transitions, error counters, and physical connection. Health diagnosis does not redefine the bit layout of PeripheralStatus.

documents.title: Firmware and Runtime Health Inspection
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Firmware and runtime health inspection reviews reboot counters, watchdog resets, crash logs, process uptime, memory pressure, and the most recent successful telemetry cycle. These observations support diagnosis but do not independently prove root cause.

documents.title: Last-saved Property Snapshot Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. A property snapshot is the last saved state known to the platform. Historical snapshot values are not live telemetry unless timestamps are fresh. queriedAt is query time; snapshotUpdatedAt is the stored snapshot update time.

documents.title: Thing-model Event History Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. Thing-model event history contains device event records returned by the event feed. It is not an alarm feed. An empty result means no event records were returned by that query; it is not proof that no alarm condition ever occurred.

documents.title: Alarm Feed Semantics
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. An alarm feed contains alarm records generated by alarm rules, notification state, severity, and recovery information. Alarm records are distinct from generic thing-model device event history.

documents.title: Connection Retry and Reconnect Backoff
documents.content: Evaluation-only synthetic knowledge. After unexpected connection loss, retry with bounded backoff instead of a tight reconnect loop. Increase delay across repeated failures up to a configured ceiling and reset delay after stable reconnection. This passage intentionally provides no exact ceiling in seconds.
